mainProgression.description: The quintessential folk turnaround in G major relative to capo. Moving from the bright tonic G to the nostalgic relative minor Em gives the song its longing, homesick atmosphere before resolving through D and C back to G.

sectionProgressions.description: The storytelling verse progression cycles through the tonic, relative minor, dominant, and subdominant

sectionProgressions.progression: G - D - Em - C - G - D - C - G
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - V - vi - IV - I - V - IV - I
sectionProgressions.description: The anthemic chorus opens with the classic I-V-vi-IV pop-folk progression before concluding with a grounded I-V-IV-I turnaround

sectionProgressions.progression: Em - D - G - C - G - D - D7
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: vi - V - I - IV - I - V - V7
sectionProgressions.description: The bridge builds dramatic momentum on the relative minor Em and culminates on a tension-filled dominant D7
Open position G major scale run demonstrating melodic embellishments and fills around cowboy chord shapes

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic chord providing the grounded, pastoral country home base
Em (vi) - Relative minor introducing bittersweet nostalgia and warmth
D (V) - Dominant chord creating natural harmonic tension pulling back to G
C (IV) - Subdominant chord adding the expansive, uplifting lift in the chorus

techniques.name: Alternating Bass Note Strumming (Boom-Chick)
techniques.description: Classic country and folk acoustic rhythm technique where you pick the individual bass root note on beat 1, strum treble strings on beat 2, pick the alternating fifth on beat 3, and strum on beat 4

notes: G: Pick low E string (3rd fret), strum, pick open D string, strum
Em: Pick low E string (open), strum, pick A string (2nd fret), strum
C: Pick A string (3rd fret), strum, pick low E or D string, strum
D: Pick open D string, strum, pick open A string, strum
sequence: Isolate the thumb or pick on the designated bass string for each chord
Follow immediately with a relaxed downward brush across the top 3-4 strings
Maintain a steady boom-chick-boom-chick pulse throughout the verses
tips: Keep your wrist loose and bouncy rather than rigid
Do not hit all 6 strings on the 'chick' strum — brush just the B, G, and D strings for clarity
Use a medium gauge pick (0.60mm - 0.73mm) for balanced acoustic attack and warmth

techniques.name: Open Cowboy Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Smooth, rhythmic transitions between fundamental open chords with anchor fingers to keep campfire rhythm seamless

notes: Use your ring finger as a guide between G and C chords
When moving from G to Em, keep your index and middle fingers poised near the 2nd fret
Move cleanly into D without pausing the right hand strumming hand
sequence: Form the full open G shape (3-2-0-0-0-3 or 3-2-0-0-3-3)
Switch cleanly to Em (0-2-2-0-0-0) on beat 1 of the new bar
Move into standard open D (X-X-0-2-3-2) with minimal fretting hand tension
Transition to C (X-3-2-0-1-0) without letting individual notes buzz
tips: Never stop your strumming hand if you miss a finger — rhythm comes before perfection
Plant your fretting fingers together simultaneously rather than one by one
Practice shifting between G and Em with eyes closed to develop muscle memory

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: John Denver introduces the iconic song with an intimate acoustic rhythm guitar strumming through the open G chord relative to capo.
notes: Place capo on the 2nd fret of your acoustic guitar
Hit the low G bass note on string 6 followed by light down-up strums
Establish the gentle 82 BPM walking tempo
sections.exerciseLabel: John Denver Acoustic G-Chord Folk Groove

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse accompanies the evocative lyrics with alternating bass notes on the G, Em, D, and C chord progression.
notes: Start with G for one bar, transitioning smoothly to Em
Keep the bass note on beat 1 prominent and authoritative
Cleanly resolve from C back into G to conclude the stanza

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The unforgettable sing-along chorus opens up with full, ringing acoustic strumming across G, D, Em, and C.
sections.progression: G - D - Em - C - G - D - C - G
notes: Open up the dynamic level — let all strings ring out fully
Emphasize the emotional high point on the Em and C chords
Rhythmic pulse stays rock steady to support campfire group singing

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: The bridge builds tension with a driving rhythm over Em and D, building into D7 before the final triumphant chorus reprise.
sections.progression: Em - D - G - C - G - D - D7
notes: Build intensity steadily through the bridge
The D7 chord adds essential bluesy dominant tension before resolving
Crescendo your right-hand strumming into the final chorus drop

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Two-octave G major scale study in open position connecting the fundamental notes of the Country Roads chord melody.
notes: Use alternate picking (down-up-down-up) across all 6 strings
Keep open strings ringing clearly without muting
Listen for the chord tones (G, B, D) embedded inside the scale run
sections.exerciseLabel: Open G Major Folk Scale Practice

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 or Gibson Hummingbird Dreadnought Acoustic
alternatives: Any steel-string acoustic guitar with a standard guitar capo
guitar.pickup: Natural acoustic resonance or under-saddle piezo pickup

amp.recommended: Acoustic amplifier (Fishman Loudbox Mini or AER Compact 60)
alternatives: Direct to PA via high-quality DI box
Clean channel on any combo amplifier

effects.reverb: Subtle hall or plate reverb for acoustic ambiance
effects.other: Quality guitar capo placed firmly behind the 2nd fret

beginner.title: Master the Open Chords and Capo
steps: Clamp your capo on the 2nd fret and check that all 6 strings ring clearly
Learn the open shapes: G, Em, C, D, and D7 relative to the capo
Practice smooth transitions between G and Em, then C and D at 60 BPM
Strum one downstroke per beat to memorize the verse and chorus order

intermediate.title: Develop the Alternating Bass Boom-Chick Strum
steps: Incorporate isolated bass note picking on beats 1 and 3 with light treble strums on 2 and 4
Practice the bass string target jumps: 6th string for G/Em, 5th string for C, 4th string for D
Bring the tempo up to the authentic recording speed of 82 BPM with a metronome
Work through the complete song structure including verse, chorus, and bridge without stopping

advanced.title: Campfire Performance & Melodic Embellishments
steps: Sing lead vocals while maintaining unwavering boom-chick rhythm
Add subtle hammer-on embellishments on the open C chord (hammering 2nd fret on the D string)
Incorporate walking bass note transitions between G and Em (G - F# - E)
Command dynamic volume shifts between whisper-quiet verses and full-voiced choruses

commonMistakes: Placing the capo directly over the fret wire or crooked, causing string buzz and tuning issues
Strumming all six strings on the D chord instead of keeping the low E and A strings silent
Rushing the tempo — 82 BPM is relaxed and swinging, not hurried
Losing the alternating bass line by strumming full chord blocks on every beat
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Capo check and open chord tuning verification
5 minutes: Isolated boom-chick alternating bass pattern on G and C chords
5 minutes: Practicing the chorus turnaround (G - D - Em - C) with steady metronome clicks
5 minutes: Bridge transition into D7 and resolving back to G
5 minutes: Full run-through singing along with the rhythm track
focusAreas: Precise thumb/pick bass note targeting on beats 1 and 3
Seamless chord changes without dropping the pulse
Clean capo intonation and fret clearance
Dynamic acoustic volume balance between verse and chorus
metronomeWork: Start at 60 BPM practicing alternating bass notes on quarter beats
Increase by 4 BPM intervals up to 82 BPM
Practice setting the metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural acoustic swing
Record your practice to check that your rhythm stays rock solid when changing between G and C
